The year was 1976. "People were looking for a party," recalls Curt Lewis, who in 1976 had just finished his journalism degree at Wichita State. "Vietnam was just over in '75. Watergate was over. Nixon was gone," he says. "Everyone was looking for a good time."

In honor of the bicentennial, trains and airplanes were painted red, white and blue. A fleet of tall ships sailed down the Hudson River. And there was a horse race unlike any other. It was called the Great American Horse Race, and it would span nearly 100 days and 3,500 miles, starting in New York, heading to Missouri, and then following the Pony Express route to California.

The rider who covered the distance fastest would get $25,000 – worth about $100,000 in today’s dollars. About 100 riders signed up. Cowboys took a break from rodeos. World War II veterans, finished with their missions on submarines and B-17 bombers, also entered. So did a sheriff — and even an Austrian count.

And then there was Virl Norton. He was one of the oldest riders. He didn't have as big a bank account as most of the others. He didn't have any fancy horse equipment. Or a big crew to help him set up camp or cook or do laundry. [...] It was the Great American Horse Race, but Virl Norton entered...a mule.

On May 31, 1976, the Great American Horse Race began. The race was structured like the Tour de France. There was a set course for each day — usually about 35 miles — and the riders were clocked at the start and finish. At first, Virl's strategy didn't pay off. ...[A]s the days went on, more and more horses started breaking down. And more and more riders started getting penalty time.

And with a focused crew and a healthy ride, sure enough... about a quarter of the way into the race, in Kankakee, Illinois, Virl Norton and Leroy (his mule) went out ahead of all the Arabians.

And so, days before the finish, it became clear that a mule was going to win the Great American Horse Race.

Source: How A Steeplejack, A Teenager And A Mule Won The Great American Horse Race, Martin Kessler, WUBR
